1 About this book

This book is by Alexy Khrabrov, with Claude as co-author. The ideas are Alexy’s: why the fork exists, what semantic sync and semantic diff should do, the shuttle-disk workflow, packing directories into SQLite archives, and the decisions recorded in these chapters. Claude Opus 5.5, an Anthropic model, wrote the text and the code with him, as the essay in this book describes. Where the text says “the user”, it means Alexy. Where it says “Unison session” or “Photo session”, it means two LLM sessions whose written records this book draws on.

The book describes the state of the fork’s master branch on 2026-11-10, at commit d6a0005d, together with the separate packdir and tiffgraph projects and dng-compare’s OCaml archive tool. The first edition, of 2026-10-31, was written before the real mirror finished; the second, of 2026-11-02, added its results, preservation of APFS clones, and the DNG walker’s move into tiffgraph. Edition 1.2 followed dng-compare’s unified archive layout and its versions across shuttle cycles, and recorded the contract the two projects agreed on. This one, 1.3, adds skeleton versions: the versions a synchronization replaces, kept as a few kilobytes each. That chapter and its code were written with Claude Fable 5.2, and its figures come from runs on six real files made while writing. Every command option was checked against the source, and the worked examples in the chapters on semantic diff and packdir are real runs on small synthetic trees, made while writing. Numbers about the benchmark and the mirror come from the two sessions’ mailbox and the design documents. This session did not take those measurements and did not touch the disks involved.

Three kinds of statement appear below, and they are kept apart:

  • Measured figures are quoted from a record, with the conditions under which they were taken.
  • Estimates are marked as estimates. Several early ones turned out to be wrong, and the book says which.
  • Unknown things are said to be unknown. In the first edition the most important was whether the real mirror of 3.6 million files would bear out the estimates. It has now finished, and the benchmark chapter gives its numbers.

The contribution policy of upstream Unison does not allow LLM-generated text or code in that project, so nothing here is meant for upstream. See Why the fork exists.

1.1 Where it fits

This book is one of nine on the FirstPair photo tools. Each owns one part, and The FirstPair Photo Stack shows how they fit together.

  • tiffgraph walks a TIFF or DNG file’s structure under a fixed grammar and finds its editable XMP packet.
  • phidentify computes a photo’s identities: SHA-256, DNG raw blocks, image data, block marks, Lightroom fingerprint, metadata record and preserved digest, and the skeleton that rebuilds a file from an edited copy.
  • phindex keeps those identities and a skeleton for every file of a volume, aligns two volumes by content, and restores a file as it was before a metadata edit.
  • DNG Compare compares pairs and preserves one side byte for byte as deltas against the other, restorable even after the other side is edited, with a searchable metadata section, through dngc.
  • Semantic Unison synchronizes photo trees, sending metadata edits without resending image bytes, keeps the versions it replaces as small skeletons, and preserves what a shuttle disk brings into the same archives.
  • packdir keeps directories of small files as SQLite archives that still work like plain files.
  • Tursolite is the SQLite and Turso layer under packdir, DNG Compare and Mechanic.
  • diskproxy serves a folder as a virtual disk, such as previews with camera metadata spliced in, and captures ratings into sidecars.
  • Lightroom Repair repairs Lightroom Classic catalogs, previews and Sync without forging their state.
